introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, "Answer all Questions"): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**DATA ANALYSIS** (Section II, 30 minutes)

A student investigated the variation of potential difference ($V$) and the current ($I$) through a semiconductor diode and obtained the following results:

| $I$ / $10^{-4}\ \mathrm{A}$ | $V$ / mV |
|---|---|
| 0.004 | 255 |
| 0.016 | 315 |
| 0.036 | 345 |
| 0.089 | 385 |
| 0.182 | 410 |
| 0.552 | 455 |
| 0.903 | 475 |
| 1.400 | 495 |
| 1.820 | 505 |
| 2.230 | 515 |

*Table 1*

The equation relating $I$ and $V$ is

$$I = I_0\,e^{\beta V}\qquad (1)$$

where $I_0$ and $\beta$ are constants.
incertitudes: Question 7 : l'en-tête de la première colonne du tableau est imprimé « 1/x 10^-4 A » (lecture d'une cellule mal rendue) ; il est lu « I / x 10^-4 A », donc I exprimé en unités de 10^-4 A, ce qui est cohérent avec l'ordre de grandeur des valeurs et avec I0 de l'ordre de 10^-10 A. Le symbole de la constante de l'équation (1) est lu comme la lettre grecque bêta. Le graphe (a) est à tracer par le candidat : le corrigé donne la grandeur à porter (ln I en fonction de V), le tableau des valeurs, les échelles et la lecture du gradient et de l'ordonnée à l'origine, sans figure de corrigé. Les dix points sont presque parfaitement alignés (beta = 24,6 par volt, I0 = 7,3 x 10^-10 A, coefficient de corrélation 0,9998).
Question 7 : le sujet n'imprime pas de total ; les marques par bloc donnent 11 + 8 + 1 = 20. `points` de l'exercice laissé vide, ceux des sous-questions repris tels qu'imprimés.

questions.enonce_markdown: Plot a suitable graph from which $\beta$ and $I_0$ could be obtained. *[11 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Choosing the graph.** Take natural logarithms of equation (1):
$$\ln I = \ln I_0 + \beta V$$
This has the form $y = c + mx$ with $y = \ln I$ and $x = V$. So plot **$\ln I$ (vertical axis) against $V$ (horizontal axis)**: a straight line with **gradient $= \beta$** and **intercept on the $\ln I$ axis $= \ln I_0$**.

**Table of values** (to be calculated by the candidate; $I$ is expressed in units of $10^{-4}\ \mathrm{A}$, so the logarithm is of a pure number):

| $V$ / mV | 255 | 315 | 345 | 385 | 410 | 455 | 475 | 495 | 505 | 515 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $I$ / $10^{-4}\ \mathrm{A}$ | 0.004 | 0.016 | 0.036 | 0.089 | 0.182 | 0.552 | 0.903 | 1.400 | 1.820 | 2.230 |
| $\ln\left(I/10^{-4}\ \mathrm{A}\right)$ | -5.52 | -4.14 | -3.32 | -2.42 | -1.70 | -0.59 | -0.10 | 0.34 | 0.60 | 0.80 |

($\log_{10}I$ may be used instead; the gradient is then $\beta\log_{10}e$.)

**The graph (to be drawn by the candidate).** Label the axes $V/\mathrm{mV}$ and $\ln(I/10^{-4}\ \mathrm{A})$; choose scales that use more than half of each axis (for example horizontal $0$ to $550\ \mathrm{mV}$ with $50\ \mathrm{mV}$ per large square, so that the line can be extended back to $V = 0$; vertical $-12$ to $+1$); plot the ten points accurately, with a small cross or a circled dot; draw a **best-fit straight line** through them (the points lie very close to a straight line, correlation coefficient $0.9998$) and **extend it to the $\ln I$ axis** at $V = 0$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Determine the values for the constants $\beta$ and $I_0$. *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Gradient $= \beta$.** Use a large triangle on the best-fit line, with points taken from the line (not from the table), for example $(250\ \mathrm{mV},\ -5.68)$ and $(520\ \mathrm{mV},\ 0.96)$:
$$\beta = \frac{0.96-(-5.68)}{(520-250)\ \mathrm{mV}} = \frac{6.64}{270\ \mathrm{mV}} = 2.46\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{mV^{-1}} = 24.6\ \mathrm{V^{-1}}$$

**Intercept $= \ln I_0$.** The best-fit line extended to $V = 0$ cuts the vertical axis at
$$\ln\left(\frac{I_0}{10^{-4}\ \mathrm{A}}\right) = -11.8$$
so
$$I_0 = e^{-11.8}\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{A} = 7.5\times10^{-6}\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{A} \approx 7\times10^{-10}\ \mathrm{A}$$

(Check with a point of the line, $V = 455\ \mathrm{mV}$, $\ln I = -0.59$: $\ln I_0 = -0.59 - 0.0246\times455 = -11.8$, which gives the same $I_0$. A least-squares fit of the ten points gives $\beta = 24.6\ \mathrm{V^{-1}}$ and $I_0 = 7.3\times10^{-10}\ \mathrm{A}$; values within a few per cent are accepted.)

**$\beta \approx 24.6\ \mathrm{V^{-1}}$ (that is $0.0246\ \mathrm{mV^{-1}}$) and $I_0 \approx 7\times10^{-10}\ \mathrm{A}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the physical significance of $I_0$? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: $I_0$ is the **reverse saturation current** of the diode: the very small current (here of the order of $10^{-10}\ \mathrm{A}$) due to thermally generated minority charge carriers, that flows when the junction is reverse biased and which equation (1) predicts at $V \to 0$ as the value from which the forward current grows exponentially.
